title: Chilika, one shore at a time
eyebrow: Birds · crossings · life beside the lagoon
intro: A shape in the reeds becomes a bird. An island carries a story. A meal opens a conversation about the water beside you. Choose the Chilika that calls to you, and give that shore time.
return_text: Find the birds, island stories and lakeside lives connected to this discovery.

chapters.title: Let the smallest movement catch your eye.
chapters.text: Begin with the reeds, then look again. Birdwatching rewards the pause between one glimpse and the next. At Mangalajodi, ask a local guide to help you notice a feeding bird, a familiar call or a seasonal visitor. Leave with a few things you can recognise, rather than a list you have hurried through.
chapters.prompt: Plan around November–February for migratory birds. Confirm the exact meeting point, guide, boat arrangements and return before travelling. Keep quiet, give wildlife space and avoid sharing sensitive nesting locations.

chapters.title: A crossing with a story on the other shore.
chapters.text: Read Kalijai’s story before you cross. The island shrine belongs to living belief; the legend is a way people remember and understand the place, not a verified account of an event. Let the water and the visit have their own time. Barkul is the departure area to investigate for this crossing.
chapters.prompt: Confirm the departure jetty, destination, return arrangement, weather decision and suitable lifejackets with the operator. A stay described as Barkul or Rambha does not establish a departure from either property.

chapters.title: Make room for what the water may reveal.
chapters.text: Choose Satapada for its own stretch of the lagoon. Irrawaddy dolphins are associated with this side of Chilika, but an outing can be worthwhile without a sighting. Watch the changing water and allow wildlife to remain wild. This is a separate starting point from a Kalijai crossing.
chapters.prompt: Agree the route and return point before boarding. Ask how the operator avoids chasing or crowding dolphins. Confirm any transfer to a Rajhans-area stay separately; the area name is not a transport booking.

chapters.title: Keep a little room for the table.
chapters.place: Lakeside food · ask where you are
chapters.text: A meal can continue the conversation begun on the water. Ask what is being cooked, how it is prepared here and what the person serving it wants you to know. Explore the lagoon’s food stories, then choose from what is actually available where you stop. The photograph is a past serving, not a promise of today’s plate.
chapters.prompt: Check today’s menu, ingredients, price and dietary needs with the kitchen. Ask before photographing people at work. A dish’s association with Chilika does not establish where its ingredients were caught or produced.

preparation.title: Choose one gateway first
preparation.text: Mangalajodi, Barkul and Satapada are different starting points. Begin with one focus; arrange road transfers separately if combining them. These chapters are choices to explore, not a one-day circuit.

preparation.title: Let the season guide the plan
preparation.text: November–February is the official Mangalajodi guide’s migratory-bird window. Check the forecast and local boat advice for your dates. A seasonal recommendation cannot guarantee birds, dolphins or a crossing.

preparation.title: Ask about the whole outing
preparation.text: Confirm boarding steps, assistance, seating, toilets, shade and the return journey. Ask about suitable lifejackets and cancellation arrangements before committing. Current services and accessibility have not been checked locally.
